# Use a standard Ubuntu 22.04 base image
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Define the final application working directory
ENV APP_DIR=/app

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps in one layer to optimize image size
# within the constraint of a single-stage build. It includes:
# 1. Installing build and runtime dependencies.
# 2. Configuring OpenMPI for containerized environments.
# 3. Downloading and building METIS from source.
# 4. Downloading and building HYPRE from source.
# 5. Downloading and building MFEM from source, linking against METIS and HYPRE.
# 6. Downloading and building the Laghos application against MFEM.
# 7. Copying the final executable and data files to their destination.
# 8. Cleaning up build dependencies and temporary files.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    git \
    wget \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && \
    # Configure OpenMPI for container environments like Docker and Kubernetes.
    # This ensures MPI processes can communicate over the primary virtual network interface.
    echo "btl_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "oob_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    \
    # --- Build Third-Party Libraries (TPLs) in /tmp ---
    BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # --- Build METIS 4.0.3 ---
    # METIS is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The OPTFLAGS are necessary to avoid build failures with modern GCC versions.
    wget -qO- https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library/header as METIS 4.0.3 lacks a 'make install' target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    # HYPRE is a parallel linear solver library required by MFEM.
    # Reverting to a simple in-source build to resolve Makefile generation issues.
    wget -qO- https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    # MFEM is the finite element library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel (MPI) version.
    # MFEM_USE_METIS_5=NO is critical when using METIS v4.x.
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    # Explicitly point MFEM to dependency locations to ensure a reliable build.
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES MFEM_USE_METIS_5=NO HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    # With all dependencies built, we now compile the main application.
    # We point it to the MFEM build directory.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    \
    # --- Stage Final Artifacts ---
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard location in the system PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Create the application directory and copy the necessary runtime data files into it.
    mkdir -p ${APP_DIR} && \
    cp -r data/* ${APP_DIR}/ && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove the temporary build directory and all build-only dependencies to
    # keep the final container image as small as possible.
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    apt-get remove -y \
        build-essential \
        g++ \
        git \
        wget \
        make \
        libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get autoremove -y && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the final working directory where the application data is located.
# This allows running Laghos with relative paths to its mesh files.
WORKDIR ${APP_DIR}

# The container is now ready. The main executable is 'laghos' on the PATH.
# Example usage:
# docker run <image_name> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.8

# Use a standard Ubuntu 22.04 base image
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Define the final application working directory
ENV APP_DIR=/app

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps in one layer to optimize image size
# within the constraint of a single-stage build. It includes:
# 1. Installing build and runtime dependencies.
# 2. Configuring OpenMPI for containerized environments.
# 3. Downloading and building METIS from source.
# 4. Downloading and building HYPRE from source.
# 5. Downloading and building MFEM from source, linking against METIS and HYPRE.
# 6. Downloading and building the Laghos application against MFEM.
# 7. Copying the final executable and data files to their destination.
# 8. Cleaning up build dependencies and temporary files.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    git \
    wget \
    make \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && \
    # Configure OpenMPI for container environments like Docker and Kubernetes.
    # This ensures MPI processes can communicate over the primary virtual network interface.
    echo "btl_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "oob_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    \
    # --- Build Third-Party Libraries (TPLs) in /tmp ---
    BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # --- Build METIS 4.0.3 ---
    # METIS is a graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # The OPTFLAGS are necessary to avoid build failures with modern GCC versions.
    wget -qO- https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz | tar -xzf - && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # Manually install library/header as METIS 4.0.3 lacks a 'make install' target.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    # HYPRE is a parallel linear solver library required by MFEM.
    # Reverting to a simple in-source build to resolve Makefile generation issues.
    wget -qO- https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz | tar -xzf - && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    # MFEM is the finite element library on which Laghos is based.
    # We build the parallel (MPI) version.
    # MFEM_USE_METIS_5=NO is critical when using METIS v4.x.
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    # Explicitly point MFEM to dependency locations to ensure a reliable build.
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES MFEM_USE_METIS_5=NO HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    # With all dependencies built, we now compile the main application.
    # We point it to the MFEM build directory.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${BUILD_DIR}/mfem && \
    \
    # --- Stage Final Artifacts ---
    # Copy the compiled executable to a standard location in the system PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # Create the application directory and copy the necessary runtime data files into it.
    mkdir -p ${APP_DIR} && \
    cp -r data/* ${APP_DIR}/ && \
    \
    # --- Cleanup ---
    # Remove the temporary build directory and all build-only dependencies to
    # keep the final container image as small as possible.
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    apt-get remove -y \
        build-essential \
        g++ \
        git \
        wget \
        make \
        libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get autoremove -y && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the final working directory where the application data is located.
# This allows running Laghos with relative paths to its mesh files.
WORKDIR ${APP_DIR}

# The container is now ready. The main executable is 'laghos' on the PATH.
# Example usage:
# docker run <image_name> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.8

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the 'laghos' HPC application
# on a single Kubernetes node within an AWS CPU environment.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster job.
  name: laghos-fractale-aws-cpu
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to create for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 for a single-node run.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI ranks (processes) for the job.
  # This will be passed to `flux run -n 8`.
  tasks: 8

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Strict mode ensures that if the job application fails, the MiniCluster reports a failure.
    strict: true

  # Keep the pods running after the job completes for inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Define the application container to be orchestrated by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      # The command for Flux to execute. The 'flux run' prefix is added by the operator.
      # This runs the laghos executable with the specified mesh file.
      command: laghos -m cube_311_hex.mesh
      
      # Set the working directory to where the laghos executable and mesh files are located.
      workingDir: /opt/laghos

      # This container runs the application workload, it is not a submission client.
      launcher: false

      # This flag indicates that the container is part of the Flux instance.
      runFlux: true

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the 'laghos' HPC application
# on a single, powerful ARM-based AWS instance in Kubernetes.
# It addresses the 'unsatisfiable request' error by scheduling on a specific
# instance type and matching the task count to the available cores.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster job.
  name: laghos-fractale-aws-cpu-arm
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI ranks, matching the vCPU count of the targeted hpc7g.16xlarge instance.
  tasks: 64

  # Keep the pods running after the job completes for inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Strict mode ensures that if the job application fails, the MiniCluster reports a failure.
    strict: true

  # Pod specification to control scheduling and behavior.
  pod:
    # Adding a nodeSelector to ensure the job lands on a node with sufficient
    # resources (64 vCPUs), preventing the 'unsatisfiable request' error.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
    # Setting the restart policy to Never aids in debugging by preserving failed pod logs.
    restartPolicy: Never

  # Flux-specific configuration.
  flux:
    # Specify the target architecture is ARM, required for the hpc7g instance type.
    arch: "arm"
    # Override the default flux-view container to use an ARM-compatible image.
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

      # This flag indicates that the container is part of the Flux instance.

import math
from typing import Dict, Any, Literal
import json

def evaluate_laghos_run(
    total_elements: int,
    total_ranks: int,
    nodes_used: int,
    cores_per_node: int,
    memory_gb_per_node: int,
    threading_hint: int,
    current_fom: float,
    threshold: float = 0.90,
    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 1.5e6,
    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 35000.0,
    elements_per_gb: float = 1.0e6,
    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.90
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Evaluates a Laghos run and provides a high-level decision and strategic hint.

    This function acts as a "diagnostician" by analyzing the performance of a
    completed Laghos run against a theoretical model. It identifies the most
    likely bottleneck (memory, poor scaling, or hardware underutilization) and
    returns a machine-readable strategic hint for what to try next.

    Args:
        total_elements (int): The total number of mesh elements in the simulation.
        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.
        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.
        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.
        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.
        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).
        current_fom (float): The measured performance from the run, typically in FOM/second.
        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum (default 0.90).
        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 1.5e6 FOM/sec).
        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant for elements/rank needed for ~76% efficiency (default 35,000).
        elements_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (elements per GB of RAM, default 1.0e6).
        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.90).

    Returns:
        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.
    """
    if total_ranks == 0:
        return {"decision": "RETRY", "reason": "The number of tasks cannot be zero.", "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_TASKS"}

    # --- Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---
    elements_per_rank = total_elements / total_ranks
    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint
    cores_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node
    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cores_per_rank
    
    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(elements_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)
    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency
    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_cores_used

    performance_ratio = 0.0
    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:
        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom

    estimated_memory_gb = total_elements / elements_per_gb
    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used) if nodes_used > 0 else 0
    
    metrics = {
        "performance_ratio": round(performance_ratio, 3),
        "scaling_efficiency": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),
        "memory_utilization": round(memory_utilization, 3),
        "elements_per_rank": int(elements_per_rank),
        "theoretical_max_fom_per_sec": f"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}"
    }

    # --- Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---
    
    if performance_ratio >= threshold:
        return {
            "decision": "STOP",
            "reason": f"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }
    
    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The number of elements is too large for the allocated memory.",
            "strategy_hint": "DECREASE_ELEMENTS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for "low" efficiency
         return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the number of elements per rank is too small (communication-bound).",
            "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_ELEMENTS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }
    
    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Hardware is not fully utilized.",
            "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_TASKS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    return {
        "decision": "RETRY",
        "reason": f"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Current configuration is reasonable but can be improved.",
        "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_ELEMENTS",
        "metrics": metrics
    }
